cf.title: Fix SSI conflicts between index-only scans and heap writes

input.subject: SSI can miss conflicts between index-only scans and heap writes

verdict_reasoning: The problem is stated with a reproducer and is a correctness bug in SERIALIZABLE, so levels 1a and 1b pass. The one surviving objection, maintenance-fit-1, is a fixable design point: the proposal does not state the new ordering rule or say which other paths that clear the all-visible bit must follow it. Someone who knows SSI and the visibility map has to confirm that the two rechecks close the race. No one but the author has posted.

brief.title: Fix missed SSI conflicts between index-only scans and heap writes
brief.problem: Two SERIALIZABLE transactions can both commit with reads that match no serial order. An index-only scan can skip the heap buffer lock while the visibility-map bit is still set, so heap_delete()/heap_update() can miss its predicate lock. A writer can also clear the bit between the reader's VM check and PredicateLockPage().
brief.proposed_design: After heap_delete()/heap_update() clear an all-visible bit, they run a second conflict-in check outside the critical section and before releasing the heap buffer lock. A SERIALIZABLE index-only scan in heapam_index_getnext_slot() rechecks the VM bit after PredicateLockPage() and fetches the heap if the bit was cleared. The author says both changes are needed.
user_visible_surface: Under SERIALIZABLE, some schedules that now commit will abort one transaction with SQLSTATE 40001.
New injection-point isolation test index_only_scan_ssi in src/test/modules/injection_points.
author_claims: Reproduced on master at 374522aa63a with GDB, for both writer-side and reader-side windows, with DELETE and UPDATE.
With the fix, all four test cases abort one transaction with 40001.
READ COMMITTED and REPEATABLE READ behaviour under the same schedules does not change.
make check, the core isolation suite and the injection_points tests pass.
brief.thread_state: Only the author has posted, sending v2 and v3 for test fixes; no one else has replied. CFbot flagged the patch as needing rebase on 2026-10-06, after v3.
unclear: The proposal gives no cost for the extra conflict check and VM recheck on write-heavy or index-only-scan-heavy workloads.
The commit message does not say what changes in visibilitymap.c.
The proposal does not say which supported branches have the bug or whether it should be back-patched.
The proposal does not say whether other paths that clear the VM bit, such as heap_lock_tuple or heap_insert, have the same race.
The proposal does not say whether other table or index access methods using index-only scans need the same fix.

objections.title: Correctness rests on a writer-side ordering rule that nothing enforces
objections.failure_scenario: A later patch adds or reworks a heap path that clears an all-visible bit, for example a new update fast path, and omits the second conflict-in check. Every existing test still passes, and SERIALIZABLE users again commit anomalous schedules. Nobody notices until another GDB-driven report arrives.
objections.argument: The fix adds a second conflict check at two call sites, heap_delete() and heap_update(), and pairs it with a reader-side recheck. The commit message does not state the new invariant: any code that clears an all-visible bit while a predicate lock could be taken must recheck afterwards. The proposal also does not say whether other VM-clearing paths, or table AMs that support index-only scans, must follow the same rule. Nothing turns this rule into an assertion or a shared helper.
objections.author_must_show: Can the invariant be stated in a comment and put into one helper or assertion that every VM-clearing path must use, with the other paths checked against it?

critic.reasoning: Per-call-site conflict checks are existing practice in heapam.c, so the request for a shared helper or assertion is weak. The proposal still does not state the new ordering rule or say whether other paths that clear the all-visible bit, or other table AMs, need it.

touch_points.label: ABI / extension API
touch_points.reason: The patch touches visibilitymap.c without saying what changes; other table AMs with index-only scans may need the same rule.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: This is a bug fix for SERIALIZABLE, but the proposal does not say which supported branches have the bug.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: Every heap path that clears an all-visible bit must now repeat the conflict-in check, and nothing enforces that.

touch_points.label: performance on the hot path
touch_points.reason: heap_delete(), heap_update() and SERIALIZABLE index-only scans get an extra check; no measurement is given.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: Which other paths that clear an all-visible bit, such as heap_insert or heap_lock_tuple, have the same race, and why are they safe if left unchanged?
Can the commit message and a code comment state the new ordering rule between clearing the all-visible bit and the conflict-in check?
Which supported branches have the bug, and is the patch meant for back-patching?
What changes in visibilitymap.c, and does it alter any exported function signature?
What does the second conflict-in check and the VM recheck cost on an update-heavy workload and on a SERIALIZABLE index-only-scan workload?

committability.owner_note: Someone who knows the SSI predicate-lock code and the heap visibility-map locking rules would have to own this.
committability.liability: The owner signs for the correctness of SERIALIZABLE with index-only scans, on every branch that receives the fix, and for any new serialization failures or lock-ordering problems it causes.
committability.author_follow_up: The author posted v2 and v3 within nine days to fix test failures; no rebase is visible since CFbot flagged the patch on 2026-10-06.

priority.reason: The bug affects users who rely on SERIALIZABLE, and the patch is small, about 19 KiB with tests. It touches heapam.c and SSI ordering, which few reviewers can sign off, and no one has replied in the thread.

provisional_note: Without the code, this review cannot confirm that the two rechecks close both windows, that the writer-side check is safe where it runs, or what the visibilitymap.c change does.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Fix buffer pinning logic/visibility bugs in [SP-]Gist Index-Only Scans
precedents_retrieved.authors: Peter Geoghegan (pgeoghegan), Michail Nikolaev (nkey), Matthias van de Meent (mmeent), Mihail Nikalayeu (mihailnikalayeu)
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch fixes a race in GiST and SP-GiST index-only scans, where concurrent VACUUM can remove a TID and set the visibility map bit before the scan checks it, so a dead tuple is returned. Later versions drop the idea of holding pins on index pages: they add a table AM API (table_index_vischeck_tuples) so the index AM checks the visibility map while it still holds the page pin, and they also change nbtree to use it.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. The last visible message (v14, December 2025) only fixes a CFBot failure, and the entry was withdrawn about six months later with no visible objection or explanation. The author had moved a backpatchable version of the fix to a separate thread.

precedents_retrieved.title: Use tuple-level SIREAD locks for index-only scans
precedents_retrieved.summary: Index-only scans that skip the heap would take tuple-level SIREAD locks instead of locking the whole heap page, with a fix to the outdated comment in nodeIndexonlyscan.c. A later experimental patch also skipped the btree page lock when the scan uses equality quals on all key columns of a unique index.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The patch stopped applying after a collision in the test files, and Daniel Gustafsson asked for a rebased version. No new version appears in the visible messages, so the entry was returned with feedback. Earlier, David Rowley found that deferrable unique constraints broke the btree lock skip, and Thomas Munro fixed that case in v4. Thomas Munro was still unsure the fix covered every case.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: This patch now fails to apply, probably due to a mostly trivial collision with fdd88571454e2b00dbe446e8609c6e4294ca89ae in the test files.

precedents_retrieved.title: Fix index-only scan plans, take 2.
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Fix index-only scan plans, take 2.
Reverted commit(s): Fix index-only scan plans when not all index columns can be returned.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
Commit 4ace45677 failed to fix the problem fully, because the
same issue of attempting to fetch a non-returnable index column
can occur when rechecking the indexqual after using a lossy index
operator.  Moreover, it broke EXPLAIN for such indexquals (which
indicates a gap in our test cases :-().

Revert the code changes of 4ace45677 in favor of adding a new field
to struct IndexOnlyScan, containing a version of the indexqual that
can be executed against the index-returned tuple without using any
non-returnable columns.  (The restrictions imposed by check_index_only
guarantee this is possible, although we may have to recompute indexed
expressions.)  Support construction of that during setrefs.c
processing by marking IndexOnlyScan.indextlist entries as resjunk
if they can't be returned, rather than removing them entirely.
(We could alternatively require setrefs.c to look up the IndexOptInfo
again, but abusing resjunk this way seems like a reasonably safe way
to avoid needing to do that.)

This solution isn't great from an API-stability standpoint: if there
are any extensions out there that build IndexOnlyScan structs directly,
they'll be broken in the next minor releases.  However, only a very
invasive extension would be likely to do such a thing.  There's no
change in the Path representation, so typical planner extensions
shouldn't have a problem.

As before, back-patch to all supported branches.

precedents_retrieved.title: Index Only Scan for index expressions
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch extends the planner so that index-only scans can be used when a query's target list or restriction clauses contain expressions that exactly match index expression columns, not only plain attribute columns. Matching requires the expression tree (or a subtree) to be identical to the index expression; no normalization of commutative or associative operators is attempted.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Testing of the sixth patch version by Vladimir Sitnikov found an error ("variable not found in subplan target list") when queries access non-indexed columns alongside an expression index. Robert Haas marked the entry Returned with Feedback because these bugs precluded committing it before the CommitFest ended, while inviting resubmission and saying the effort was good.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Based on this report, this patch appears to have bugs that would
preclude committing it, so I'm marking it "Returned with Feedback" for
this CommitFest, which is due to end shortly.

precedents_retrieved.title: Index Only Scan support for cube
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a GiST fetch function for the cube extension so that queries on cube columns can use Index Only Scans. It reuses g_cube_decompress() as the fetch function, since both only need to detoast the key.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author withdrew it as obsolete after commit d3a4f89 (Allow no-op GiST support functions to be omitted). He said he would work on a broader patch for contrib modules to support GiST Index Only Scans and remove no-op support functions.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Index Only Scan support for cube" patch now is obsolete.

precedents_retrieved.title: Write visibility map during CLUSTER/VACUUM FULL
precedents_retrieved.summary: Make CLUSTER and VACUUM FULL write the visibility map during heap rewrite, by having rewriteheap.c build VM pages alongside heap pages (bypassing the buffer manager) and flush them to smgr. It used its own simplified all-visible check, relying on HeapTupleSatisfiesVacuum() having already set hint bits; TOAST relations were left without a VM.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Andres Freund objected to copying visibility-map implementation details into rewriteheap.c and to adding another copy of visibility-determination logic, which he said has proven hard to get right. He also questioned part of the motivation and pointed to related prior discussion that might share logic, especially for TOAST. The author did not respond to these comments for over two months, and the entry was marked returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I don't think we should have yet another copy of logic determining
visibility. It has repeatedly proven hard to get right in the past, and
it'll not get better by having yet another copy.

precedents_retrieved.title: Write visibility map during CLUSTER/VACUUM FULL
precedents_retrieved.authors: Alexander Korotkov (smagen), Justin Pryzby (justinpryzby), Anna Akenteva (anna.akenteva), Anna Akenteva (a.akenteva)
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes CLUSTER and VACUUM FULL write the visibility map in heapam_relation_copy_for_cluster(), so the table needs no extra VACUUM afterwards. VM pages are built in RewriteStateData beside the heap pages and written straight to smgr, with an all-visible check that assumes tuples already passed HeapTupleSatisfiesVacuum().
precedents_retrieved.objection: The original author stopped responding, and no one took ownership of the patch. In 2019 the entry was returned with feedback because review comments went unanswered for more than two months. After a 2021 revival, Justin Pryzby kept rebasing it and asked for an owner, then proposed closing it, and the entry was marked returned with feedback in 2022. Open points included Amit Kapila's question about syncing VM pages at end_heap_rewrite and Justin Pryzby's note that pg_class.relallvisible is not set.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I'm planning to close this patch until someone can shepherd it.

precedents_retrieved.title: SERIALIZABLE on standby servers
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch allows SERIALIZABLE READ ONLY DEFERRABLE transactions on standby servers by having the primary write snapshot safety information into commit records and separate WAL records. The standby waits for a point in the WAL stream where a snapshot is known to be safe, using hypothetical transactions that the primary tracks as stand-ins for standby transactions.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author called the patch prototype/WIP code with unsolved problems. Two of them are a race between the safety decision and the order of commit records in WAL, and the absence of snapshot safety information in checkpoints. A third is that the primary makes transactions visible in ProcArrayEndTransaction() order while the standby uses commit record order, which can allow serialization anomalies. No review of the general approach came, and the entry was later withdrawn; the visible messages do not show who withdrew it.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: And that's precisely the issue: on the primary, transactions become visible to other transactions in the order in which they perform ProcArrayEndTransaction(), but on the standby, they become visible in the order in which they RecordTransactionCommit().

precedents_retrieved.title: OFFSET optimisation for IndexScan using visibility map
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch pushed OFFSET information down to index scans, so tuples on all-visible pages that the Limit node would throw away were skipped without heap fetches. The author later reworked it into a general "Index Only Fetch Scan", which evaluates filter quals from index data and fetches heap tuples only for rows it returns.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Michael Paquier marked it returned with feedback because the author promised an update in July and did not post one by October. Heikki Linnakangas objected to the redesign: evaluating expressions on index entries of deleted tuples can raise errors, such as division by zero, before the visibility check filters those entries out. The author also had no cost estimation that would avoid a 3-4% slowdown for high-correlation, low-selectivity cases. Tom Lane's review of predicate locking appears only in quoted lines.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Now, maybe there's some way around that, but I don't know what. Without some kind of a solution, this won't work.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert "Avoid the creation of the free space map for small heap relations".
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert "Avoid the creation of the free space map for small heap relations".
Reverted commit(s): Improve code comments in b0eaa4c51b.; Avoid creation of the free space map for small heap relations, take 2.; During pg_upgrade, conditionally skip transfer of FSMs.; Add more tests for FSM.; Clear the local map when not used.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This feature was using a process local map to track the first few blocks
in the relation.  The map was reset each time we get the block with enough
freespace.  It was discussed that it would be better to track this map on
a per-relation basis in relcache and then invalidate the same whenever
vacuum frees up some space in the page or when FSM is created.  The new
design would be better both in terms of API design and performance.

List of commits reverted, in reverse chronological order:

06c8a5090e  Improve code comments in b0eaa4c51b.
13e8643bfc  During pg_upgrade, conditionally skip transfer of FSMs.
6f918159a9  Add more tests for FSM.
9c32e4c350  Clear the local map when not used.
29d108cdec  Update the documentation for FSM behavior..
08ecdfe7e5  Make FSM test portable.
b0eaa4c51b  Avoid creation of the free space map for small heap relations.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found. [P2] changes the SIREAD lock granularity for index-only scans and stalled on a rebase, and [P1] fixes a VACUUM and visibility-map race in GiST index-only scans with no recorded reason; neither recorded reason applies to this SSI race fix, and the thread cites no earlier discussion.

From the standards and compatibility angle there is nothing to object to. The only user-visible change is more 40001 aborts under SERIALIZABLE, which the standard requires and which SERIALIZABLE applications already have to retry. The patch adds no syntax, GUC, catalog object, pg_dump state or psql change. A committer would likely still ask which supported branches have the bug and whether the fix is meant for back-patching, but that is a question for the author, not an objection.

The proposal changes no on-disk format, WAL record, catalog, or wire protocol message: it adds an in-memory predicate-lock recheck and a visibility map bit recheck on existing paths. SERIALIZABLE does not run on hot standby, so the standby and the subscriber see no change, and the visibilitymap.c change seems to read the existing VM bit only. Without the code, I cannot check whether that change alters an exported function signature, which would matter for a back-patch.

The patch adds no privilege, role, function, view or setting, and it exposes no new data or error detail; it only adds serialization failures where SSI already should raise them. Its effect on the cost and back-patching of serializable index-only scans belongs to other angles.

The proposal fixes a real SERIALIZABLE anomaly, so desirability is not in doubt. The extra writer check runs only after an all-visible bit is cleared, and the reader recheck runs only for SERIALIZABLE index-only scans, so hot-path cost looks limited, but no measurement is given. Committability is weak because no committer who knows SSI has replied, which does not count against the idea.

This is a correctness fix for SSI inside heapam, and no existing feature, setting or extension gives serializable guarantees for index-only scans. Setting enable_indexonlyscan = off only avoids the bug, and only for users who know about it, so it is not a fix.

This is a correctness fix for SERIALIZABLE, where both transactions commit with reads that match no serial order, and it comes with a reproducer. A demand objection does not apply: every user who relies on SERIALIZABLE needs the guarantee, and no workaround keeps index-only scans. Cost to other workloads and back-patching belong to other angles.
